label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 12
knowledgePattern: Use equivalent universal rules to isolate the sole possible truth
solution:
For real x, x2<1 is equivalent to |x|<1, and x2<4 to |x|<2. Thus E is the contrapositive of A, F is the contrapositive of B, and G is equivalent to C after translating only if.

Each equivalent pair shares a truth value, so none of its members can be the unique true statement. Only D remains.

This possibility is consistent: let P mean x = 3/2. Then every x with P has |x| < 2, so D is true. C and G fail at 3/2; A, B, E and F fail at zero. Hence exactly D is true. Answer D.

hints.title: Put all the rules in one form
hints.body: Translate only if into an implication and express squared bounds as equivalent absolute-value bounds.
hints.recap: A only if B means that A implies B.
hints.pitfall: Do not replace a contrapositive with an unjustified converse.
hints.pause: Compare each rule with the contrapositive of the other rules.

recall.reminder: A only if B means that A implies B.

hints.title: Use the single-truth requirement
hints.body: Group equivalent statements and trace any implication that would force a second true statement.
hints.recap: Equivalent statements have the same truth value, so neither can stand alone as the unique truth.
hints.pitfall: An elimination argument should not accidentally leave an inconsistent set of conditions.
